CHIEF COMPLAINT
Nonhealing foot ulcer with recent redness and drainage

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with a nonhealing foot ulcer on the right foot that has been present for approximately two months. He reports the wound recently became red and began draining, which prompted his visit. He believes the ulcer originated from walking barefoot at Dewey Beach. The patient reports the ulcer sometimes throbs but denies specific sharp pain. He describes increased pressure sensation but notes this is not distinctly painful. He has not experienced drainage or redness prior to this presentation. Patient was referred by his PCP who initiated antibiotic therapy; however, patient has not yet filled the prescription and cannot recall the specific medication name, though he states he has taken it before.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies fever. Reports occasional throbbing sensation at the ulcer site without specific localized pain. Positive for drainage and redness from the ulcer. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Patient reports taking diabetes medication regularly but does not consistently monitor blood glucose levels. PCP prescribed antibiotics (name unknown, not yet filled).

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as an ambulance driver. Reports recent beach activity at Dewey Beach where he walked barefoot.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever present. Right foot examination reveals a one by two inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot, just proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. Wound demonstrates redness, drainage present, and edema surrounding the ulcer. No necrotic tissue visualized. No odor appreciated. No bony exposure noted. Palpation elicits increased pressure sensation without distinct pain.

RESULTS
Right foot X-ray: No evidence of osteomyelitis. Ankle-brachial index ordered to assess blood supply to the foot.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diabetic foot ulcer with secondary infection of the right foot. Patient's diabetes control is suboptimal with last documented A1C approximately 10. Patient instructed to follow up with PCP to optimize diabetes management. Plan includes: (1) Debridement of ulcer performed today, (2) Clindamycin 400 mg orally twice daily for seven days to treat infection, (3) Surgical shoe prescribed to reduce pressure on affected foot and prevent irritation, (4) Ankle-brachial index study ordered to assess vascular supply, (5) Follow-up appointment in two weeks for reassessment and possible repeat debridement. Patient instructed to call office with any concerns or if emergency symptoms develop (fever, black discoloration, feeling unwell), and to seek urgent care or emergency evaluation if needed.
